svg.title: Matrix Euler support tests and finite kernel transport
svg.desc: An exact support sequence has degree-one dimension equal to matrix rank. A resonant two-dimensional Jordan block has one class from the negative-side homogeneous solution and another from the central cokernel. Exact real components of its logarithmic solution and forced primitive are graphed on t=-exp(-u), 0 at most u at most 3. The full kernel complex and finite transport hypotheses are retained.
svg.text: Matrix Euler support tests
All ranks and all constant matrices · the actual real halfspace test
1. The actual fibre and its two contributions
PA = t∂ₜ − A; homogeneous solutions on the negative side form Cʳ.
0 → Cʳ / EA⁺ → H¹(VA) → TA → 0
dim EA⁺ = dim TA; therefore dim H¹(VA) = r.
Jordan block: A e₁ = 0, A e₂ = e₁; SA = C e₁, TA = C[e₂].
(0, v) comes from the side solution modulo central solutions.
(e₂, w) maps to the nonzero central forcing cokernel.
Together these two classes form H¹(VA) ≅ C². (MEC.28–MEC.30)
2. A real path in one fixed logarithm branch
t = −exp(−u), 0 ≤ u ≤ 3; log t = −u + iπ; halfdisc radius 2.
u
Re
Blue: Re v₁ = −u. Green: Re w₁ = (u² − π²)/2.
v = e₂ + (log t)e₁, PA v = 0.
w = (log t)e₂ + ½(log t)²e₁, PA w = e₂.
Only their first real coordinates are plotted; the full v and w retain both imaginary parts.
3. What a gauge must preserve
Finite operator cells keep the full kernel complex K.
K ⊗ᴸπ⁻¹D π⁻¹N ≅ μhom(Sol N, O)
An H⁰ kernel identification can vanish after derived tensor.
Actual R action + D₀-linear cutoff + finite chain homotopies
give Sol N ≅ Sol NA in the category localized at p.
Integer derivative gauge: ∂ₜ PA = PA−I ∂ₜ.
Its cone is a shifted constant complex, with no nonzero microsupport.
General kernel comparison and contact transport retain their stated hypotheses.
MEC.1–MEC.35; Solutions 3.EQ–3.ES.
Matrix Euler equality is proved here; arbitrary systems need additional arguments.
